items.value: All three - the Charter Act of 1813, the General Committee of Public Instruction of 1823 and the Orientalist-Anglicist controversy
items.reasoning: These three are successive links in a single chain. The Charter Act of 1813 first made the Company responsible for education and set aside one lakh rupees a year for it, creating the fund that had to be spent. The General Committee of Public Instruction, constituted in 1823, was the body created to spend that money and to decide the shape of instruction. Within that Committee the Orientalists, who wanted classical Indian learning supported, and the Anglicists, who wanted English and European science, deadlocked, and the controversy was resolved by Macaulay's Minute and Bentinck's resolution of 1835 in favour of English education. Each step therefore led to the introduction of English education.

items.value: Kodaikanal lake in Tamil Nadu
items.reasoning: The Kodaikanal lake is man-made, created in the 1860s by damming a stream in the valley when the hill station was developed. Kolleru is a natural freshwater lake in the deltaic tract between the Krishna and the Godavari, Nainital is a natural tectonic lake of the Kumaon hills, and Renuka is a natural lake in the Sirmaur district of Himachal Pradesh.

items.value: The All India Home Rule League
items.reasoning: Gandhi became president of the All India Home Rule League in 1920 and the organisation was renamed Swarajya Sabha, its object being restated as the attainment of swaraj by constitutional and peaceful means. The Hindu Mahasabha, the South Indian Liberal Federation (the Justice Party) and the Servants of India Society all retained their names.

items.value: Dinabandhu Mitra writing Neel Darpan, around 1858-60, is the earliest of the four
items.reasoning: Neel Darpan, the play on the oppression of indigo ryots, was written in the wake of the Indigo revolt and published in 1860. Satyendranath Tagore cleared the Indian Civil Service examination in 1863, Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875, and Bankim Chandra's Anandamath appeared in 1882. Neel Darpan therefore comes first.

items.value: Only statements 2 and 3 - groundwater pollution and a lowered water table
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong, and indeed inverted: stripping sand deepens the channel and lets tidal or saline water push further upstream, so salinity rises rather than falls, and coastal rivers subjected to heavy mining show exactly this saline ingress. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the sand bed acts as a natural filter and as the storage medium of the shallow aquifer, so removing it exposes groundwater to contamination and drops the water table, drying the wells that draw from the riverbed.

items.value: Only statement 3 is correct - irrigation over time can salinize agricultural land
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is the reverse of the truth: organic matter behaves like a sponge and markedly raises the water holding capacity of soil, which is why it is added to sandy soils. Statement 2 is wrong: soil is central to the sulphur cycle, holding sulphur in organic matter and minerals and hosting the microbes that oxidise and reduce it into plant-available sulphate. Statement 3 is correct: irrigation water carries dissolved salts, and where drainage is poor and evaporation high the salts accumulate at the surface as the water evaporates, which is the classic cause of secondary salinization.

items.value: The United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development 2012 at Rio de Janeiro (Rio+20)
items.reasoning: PAGE was set up in 2013 as the response of UN agencies to the Rio+20 outcome document, The Future We Want, in which states recognised the green economy as a means of achieving sustainable development and asked the UN system to help countries pursue it. It therefore emerged from the 2012 Rio conference rather than from the Johannesburg summit, the Paris climate conference, or a summit hosted in New Delhi.

items.value: All five listed applications
items.reasoning: Four of the five are beyond dispute: additive manufacturing is used to print chocolate, sugar and other confectionery (1); it produced the widely reported bionic ear that combined printed tissue with an electronic coil (2); it is standard in the automotive industry for prototyping and for end-use parts (3); and it makes patient-specific implants, cranial plates and surgical guides for reconstructive surgery (4). That combination settles the item by elimination, because option A omits 2, option B omits 1 and 4, and option C omits 2 and 3 - each dropping an application that is certainly real. Only the option taking in every statement survives, and the fifth is defensible on its own terms through printed circuitry, photonic and memory components. Note a printing defect in the paper: option D opens with a character set as a lowercase letter l that is plainly the digit 1.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct - Barren Island is an active volcano in Indian territory
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is the only confirmed active volcano in India. Statement 2 is wrong on its geography: the island lies roughly 140 km north-east of Port Blair in the Andamans, not east of Great Nicobar, which is far to the south of the archipelago. Statement 3 is wrong: after the 1991 eruption ended a long dormancy the volcano erupted repeatedly, including in the mid-1990s, in 2005 and again in 2017, so it has not been inactive since 1991.

items.value: It is an invasive species that reduces the biodiversity of the areas it colonises
items.reasoning: Prosopis juliflora, introduced for fuelwood and to green degraded land, has become one of India's most aggressive invasive alien plants. It forms dense thorny thickets, draws heavily on groundwater, and suppresses native grasses and trees, so that grazing land, wetlands such as Banni and protected areas lose their native species composition. That ecological damage, not any cosmetic or pesticide use, is why it is in the news.

items.value: All three statements are correct
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: reef-building corals need warm, clear, shallow water, so reefs are concentrated in the tropical belt. Statement 2 is correct: Indonesia, Australia and the Philippines between them hold well over a third of the world's reef area, each being among the largest reef nations. Statement 3 is correct: coral reefs are the most phylum-diverse habitat on earth, representing the great majority of the animal phyla, whereas tropical rainforests, although richer in the sheer number of species, contain far fewer phyla because their diversity is concentrated in insects and other arthropods.

items.value: The UNFCCC Secretariat
items.reasoning: Momentum for Change is the UNFCCC secretariat's initiative to spotlight exemplary climate action, and Climate Neutral Now, launched by the same secretariat in 2015, invites individuals and organisations to measure, reduce and offset their emissions using certified emission reductions. The IPCC assesses climate science, UNEP and the WMO run separate programmes, and none of them launched this initiative.

items.value: Only pair 2 is correct - Warren Hastings founded the Calcutta Madarsa
items.reasoning: Warren Hastings established the Calcutta Madrasa in 1781 for the study of Arabic and Persian and of Muslim law, so pair 2 holds. Pair 1 is wrong: the Sanskrit College at Benaras was founded in 1791 by Jonathan Duncan, the Resident there; William Jones founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal, which is a different institution. Pair 3 is wrong in its founder: Fort William College was set up at Calcutta in 1800 by Lord Richard Wellesley, the Governor-General, and not by his brother Arthur Wellesley, the soldier who later became Duke of Wellington.

items.reasoning: Catalonia is the autonomous community of north-eastern Spain whose independence referendum was in the news, and Mindanao is the large southern island of the Philippines that was placed under martial law during the Marawi conflict, so pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Crimea is the Black Sea peninsula of Ukraine annexed by Russia, not part of Hungary, and Oromia is the largest regional state of Ethiopia, not of Nigeria.

items.value: Air India nationalised, then Imperial Bank renamed State Bank of India, then the Kerala communist government, then Goa's liberation
items.reasoning: Air India was nationalised under the Air Corporations Act of 1953 and became the national carrier that year. The Imperial Bank of India was taken over and renamed the State Bank of India in 1955. The Communist Party formed the first democratically elected communist government in an Indian State in Kerala in 1957. Goa was liberated and became part of independent India in 1961. The sequence is therefore 3, 2, 1, 4.

items.value: Article 21 read with the other freedoms guaranteed in Part III
items.reasoning: The stem itself names the right to life and personal liberty, which is Article 21, and the constitutional holding is that privacy is intrinsic to that guarantee and also runs through the other freedoms of Part III. Article 14 concerns equality before the law and the 42nd Amendment is unconnected with privacy; Article 17 abolishes untouchability and the Directive Principles are not enforceable rights; Article 24 prohibits child labour in hazardous employment. Only option C names the provisions the statement rests on.

items.value: Barley, finger millet, groundnut and sesamum
items.reasoning: Minimum Support Prices announced on the recommendation of the CACP cover a fixed list of field crops. Barley is one of the six rabi crops on that list, and finger millet (ragi), groundnut and sesamum are among the kharif crops on it. Areca nut, coffee and turmeric are plantation, beverage and spice crops that carry no MSP; coffee is handled by the Coffee Board and arecanut and turmeric are traded without any support price.

items.value: Arunachal Pradesh
items.reasoning: Pakhui, also spelt Pakke, is a tiger reserve and wildlife sanctuary in the East Kameng district of Arunachal Pradesh, lying in the foothills of the Eastern Himalaya and adjoining Nameri across the Assam border. It is known for its hornbill nest adoption programme.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct - PSLV serves remote sensing missions and GSLV mainly communication satellites
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the PSLV places Earth observation and remote sensing satellites in polar sun-synchronous orbits, while the GSLV was developed to lift heavier communication satellites towards geosynchronous transfer orbit. Statement 2 is wrong: a satellite appears fixed in the sky only from geostationary orbit, which is the GSLV's business; PSLV payloads in low polar orbits sweep across the sky several times a day. Statement 3 is wrong: the GSLV Mk III is a three-stage vehicle using two solid strap-on boosters, a liquid core stage and a cryogenic upper stage, not a four-stage vehicle with alternating solid and liquid stages, which describes the PSLV configuration instead.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct - the associate banks were merged into the State Bank of India
items.reasoning: Statement 2 is plainly correct: the five remaining associate banks, together with the Bharatiya Mahila Bank, were merged into the State Bank of India with effect from April 2017. Statement 1 turns on the word steadily, and government recapitalisation of public sector banks over the decade did not rise steadily - it moved up and down from year to year, falling sharply in the middle of the period before the very large infusion announced under the recapitalisation package of 2017, so the trend is uneven rather than a steady increase. Read leniently as merely describing a rising overall trend, statement 1 could be defended, which would make the answer C; that is the runner-up.

items.value: Cereal grains hulled, cooked chicken eggs, and newspapers containing advertising material
items.reasoning: Hulled cereal grains are nil-rated, birds' eggs in shell are nil-rated whether fresh, preserved or cooked, and newspapers, journals and periodicals are nil-rated expressly whether or not they carry advertising material, so items 1, 2 and 4 are exempt. Fish that has been processed and canned is not: processing takes it out of the exemption available to fresh and chilled fish and it bears a positive rate, so item 3 is excluded.

items.value: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the expression critical wildlife habitat is defined in the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, as areas of national parks and sanctuaries kept inviolate for wildlife conservation. Statement 2 is correct: the Baiga of the Dindori area in Madhya Pradesh were the first community in India to be granted habitat rights under that Act. Statement 3 is wrong: habitat rights for particularly vulnerable tribal groups are claimed before the Gram Sabha and recognised through the sub-divisional and district level committees under the Forest Rights Act, administered by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, and are not declared by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

items.value: All four - birds, blowing dust, rain and wind
items.reasoning: Every one of these is a recognised agent of plant disease dispersal. Wind carries fungal spores and bacteria over long distances, blowing dust carries soil-borne inoculum and also wounds leaves so that pathogens can enter, rain splash detaches and spreads spores from lesion to leaf and washes them down the canopy, and birds move pathogens on their feet and plumage and transmit them while feeding on fruit and seed. None of the four can be excluded.

Statement 3 is correct: Sikkim was declared India's first fully organic State in 2016 after converting its entire cultivated area to organic practice.
